answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut to component spend and the primary contract expires in 14 days without auto-renew. The low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate alone, so switching primary supply is the most direct path to the cost objective. Memory c2 from day 38 records that moving primary supply to this same low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate — exactly the precedent that makes a switch the lowest-risk route to the 18% cut. The assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so the decision is bounded to a guarded scale rather than a full cutover at peak exposure: a small initial volume on the new primary, with the incumbent retained as a second source during transition. This avoids concentrating on a single supplier while the line has no slack, and keeps migration risk inside one review cycle. c2's accuracy on cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing is the load-bearing assumption here, so verifying it before committing is worth the single verification slot. No memory needs to be discarded; the memory set remains consistent.
